name: Reverse-Income Economic Viability Model
phase: Hypothesis Framing and Assumption Mapping Tactics
hypothesis: We believe this business model can achieve sustainable profitability at target scale. We will verify this by building a reverse unit-economics model, and consider it validated if the required conversion rates and average revenue per user (ARPU) remain within historical benchmark ranges for this industry vertical.

plan.label: Preparation
plan.text: Fix an ambitious revenue milestone, such as ten million in annual recurring revenue.

plan.label: Execution
plan.text: Work backward from revenue: required customers = ARR / ARPU, then conversion and acquisition cost.

plan.label: Data collection
plan.text: Check the required metrics against benchmarks: Required Leads = Target ARR / (ARPU × Funnel Conversion Rate).

planFull.label: Preparation
planFull.text: Fix an ambitious financial milestone (e.g., 10,000,000 ARR).

planFull.label: Execution
planFull.text: Work backward to calculate the necessary funnel metrics: divide target revenue by expected ARPU to determine the required customer volume, then calculate the necessary conversion rates and acquisition costs across the funnel.

planFull.label: Data collection
planFull.text: Compare required operational metrics against real-world industry benchmarks: Required Leads = Target ARR / (ARPU × Funnel Conversion Rate)

warning.label: Spreadsheet Viability Syndrome
warning.text: A model balances by inserting aggressive growth or fantasy acquisition costs, hiding an unviable business.

warningFull: Financial models can always be balanced by inserting aggressive compound growth rates or unrealistically low customer acquisition costs, masking unviable business fundamentals.
